Songkran, the Thai New Year, is a public holiday on Tuesday 13 to Thursday 15 April 2027, and on Koh Samui the street water fights usually start a day early, on Monday 12 April. Chaweng Beach Road is the main battleground, with official celebrations also in Lamai and Nathon, while beach clubs and Central Samui run their own parties. It is one of the hottest times of the year (April highs around 32 °C) and the sea is at its calmest, so it is also a very good week for boat trips.

For reference, the official 2026 programme on Samui ran from 12 to 15 April in three subdistricts: Bo Phut (which includes Chaweng and Fisherman's Village), Maret (Lamai) and Ang Thong (Nathon). The 2027 programme is normally announced in March; we expect the same pattern and will update this page when it is published. Songkran is not an alcohol-ban day.

Where to celebrate Songkran on Samui

Chaweng Beach Road

Chaweng Beach Road is Samui's biggest water fight: a few kilometres of bars, shops and hotels where everyone, from shop staff to tourists in pick-up trucks, joins in from late morning until after dark. Bars set up water barrels and speakers outside, and shops along the road sell water guns and waterproof pouches. Expect to be soaked within a minute of stepping outside. See our Chaweng guide.

Lamai

Lamai's celebration is smaller and more relaxed than Chaweng's, mostly along Lamai Beach Road. Lamai is in Maret subdistrict, one of the three official Samui venues. A good choice if you want the water without the crowds. See our Lamai guide.

Nathon (more traditional)

Nathon, Samui's main town on the west coast, hosts the Ang Thong subdistrict celebration. It is more local and more traditional, with families, temple ceremonies and processions alongside the water fights. Go in the morning for the temple rites and stay for lunch at the waterfront. See our Nathon guide.

Beach clubs and Central Samui

Beach clubs and the mall run their own Songkran events, announced a few weeks ahead. The 2025 pattern gives a fair idea of 2027: ARKbar held free beach parties for five to six nights, SEEN Beach Club at Avani Chaweng held a pool party from 13 April, Central Samui held a foam party from 12:00 to 24:00 on 13–15 April, Nikki Beach in Lipa Noi ran a Songkran brunch and Chi Samui in Bang Rak held a DJ party. Walk-in sunbeds at the big Chaweng clubs are not guaranteed during Songkran. See Koh Samui beach clubs.

Traditions behind the water

Songkran marks the sun moving into Aries and the start of the traditional Thai solar year. The water began as a gentle blessing, not a fight:

  • Rod nam dam hua: younger family members pour scented water over the hands of parents, grandparents and respected elders, asking forgiveness and receiving a blessing. It usually happens on 14 April.
  • Song nam phra: people bathe Buddha images with scented water at temples and at home.
  • Merit-making: families give food to monks at dawn and visit temples such as Big Buddha (Wat Phra Yai) and Wat Plai Laem.
  • Sand chedis (chedi sai): people carry sand into temple grounds and build small pagodas decorated with flags, returning the sand carried out on their feet over the year.
  • Din sor pong: a white, cooling paste of chalk and water that people dab on each other's faces as a blessing.

More background: Thai culture and traditions.

Songkran etiquette

  • Don't splash monks, novices, elderly people, babies or anyone in uniform on duty.
  • Never throw water at motorbike riders or drivers; it causes crashes.
  • Don't aim at faces at close range, and avoid high-pressure hoses and ice water.
  • If someone is clearly dressed for work or carrying electronics, leave them alone.
  • Apply din sor pong gently to cheeks or shoulders, never in eyes, and ask first.
  • Dress modestly: thin white clothes become see-through when wet, and topless walking on the road is offensive.
  • Smile. Getting angry about being splashed in a water-fight zone is the one real faux pas.

Safety during Songkran

Songkran's "seven dangerous days" are the deadliest week on Thai roads. Over 10–16 April 2026 there were 1,242 accidents, 1,200 injuries and 242 deaths nationwide; speeding was the leading cause, and motorcycles were involved in about two-thirds of incidents on the final day. On Samui:

  • Don't ride a scooter through water-fight zones. A bucket of water at speed blinds you, and wet roads are slippery.
  • Never drink and ride. Police set up checkpoints over Songkran.
  • Put your phone, cash and passport copy in a waterproof pouch; cheap ones leak, so double-bag.
  • Protect your eyes with swimming goggles or sunglasses; water in guns is often not clean.
  • Drink plenty of water and use sun cream: it is 32 °C and you will be in the sun all day.
  • Emergency numbers: Tourist Police 1155, ambulance 1669.

See roads on Koh Samui and precautions and safety.

What to wear and carry

  • Quick-dry shorts and a dark T-shirt or a loud Songkran flower shirt, sold everywhere in April for a few hundred baht.
  • Flip-flops or sandals with straps; roads and pavements get slippery.
  • A waterproof pouch on a neck strap for your phone, plus a zip-lock bag inside it.
  • Goggles or wraparound sunglasses.
  • Waterproof sun cream, reapplied every couple of hours.
  • A small water gun; you will be a target either way, so you may as well reply.
  • Leave at the hotel: passport, laptop, good camera, anything that can't get wet.

Getting around during Songkran

Expect slow traffic on the ring road through Chaweng and Lamai, and parts of Chaweng Beach Road become pedestrian water-fight zones. Songthaews keep running, but you will get wet in the open back, so bag your valuables. Grab cars are the driest option and work best in Chaweng, Bophut and Lamai, with surge prices at peak times. Allow extra time for airport runs on 12–15 April. More options: getting around Koh Samui.

Where to stay for Songkran

Stay in Chaweng if you want to be in the middle of it: you can walk out of your hotel straight into the water fight. Bophut and Fisherman's Village are a short Grab ride away and calmer at night. Lamai is lively but smaller. Maenam, Choeng Mon and the west coast (Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam) are quiet enough to avoid it altogether, apart from a few splashes on the ring road. Families with small children often prefer Bophut or Maenam. See where to stay on Koh Samui.

Book early

Songkran is now one of Samui's busiest weeks. After The White Lotus aired in 2025, foreign Songkran bookings for 10–17 April 2025 were up 65 % on the year before, according to hotel booking data. In 2027 Easter Sunday falls on 28 March, so the Easter rush comes about two weeks before Songkran rather than in the same week. Book flights, villas and boat trips as early as you can, especially for 12–15 April.

Boat trips over Songkran

April has some of the calmest sea of the year, with about 83 mm of rain over six days and sea temperatures around 30 °C, so it is an excellent month for island trips. Ang Thong Marine Park is open (it closes only from 1 November to 15 December). A day on the water is also a good break from three days of water fights.

  • Ang Thong speedboat tour: 1,800 THB adult, 1,400 THB child.
  • Ang Thong VIP tour: 4,500 THB, only 15 guests on a big speedboat.
  • Pig Island speedboat tour: 1,450 THB adult, 1,250 THB child.
  • Private speedboat charters for families and groups.

Hotel pickup is included from most areas of Koh Samui; Nathon, Lipa Noi, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut add 400 THB per person, return. Book a few days ahead in Songkran week. Online booking for tomorrow closes at midnight Thailand time.
